 Wet, windy weather not yet finished with B.C.'s South Coast | CBC News Loaded British Columbia Wet, windy weather not yet finished with B.C.'s South Coast
 Yet another in a series of systems is forecast to batter the region on Saturday, triggering multiple yellow warnings from Environment and Climate Change Canada. Multiple rainfall and wind warnings remain in effect for region
 Simon Little · CBC News · Posted: Nov 14, 2026 5:55 PM EST | Last Updated: 2 hours ago Play Listen to this article Estimated 3 minutes The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results. A person walks along the seawall near Coal Harbour on a rainy day in Vancouver, B.C. on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Ethan Cairns/CBC News) Social Sharing
 The wet and windy weather isn't over yet for British Columbia's South Coast.
 Yet another in a series of systems is forecast to batter the region on Saturday, triggering multiple yellow warnings from Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC).
 Days after a powerful storm prompted widespread flooding, another round of heavy rain is forecast for the Sea to Sky corridor from Squamish to Whistler.
 More stories from Vancouver-South Coast
 The entire Sea to Sky and Pemberton Valley regions remain under high streamflow advisories from the B.C. River Forecast Centre, and the Village of Pemberton remains under an evacuation alert. 
 Highway 99 was reopened east of Pemberton on Saturday night following a closure due to flooding. However, the Squamish River Road remains closed from the 3 kilometre mark to the Pikchuk Creek Bridge.
 ECCC forecasts between 40 and 70 millimetres of rain could fall by Sunday in the Sea to Sky. It warns that the ground is already saturated from previous storms — meaning its ability to absorb water could be limited, intensifying the effects of the rainfall.
 WATCH | 3 dead in boat crash on Squamish River: Boat crash kills 3 on flood-swollen B.C. river north of Vancouver
 November 13 | Duration closed caption 1:50 
 "While the flood risk is decreasing, we are anticipating more rain coming through the weekend," said Squamish Mayor Sean Easton.
 "Our rivers are dynamic and they are always changing, so we just really encourage people to be safe, stay well back from river banks, particularly keeping an eye on children and pets, and whatever you do, don't go in the water."
 A police investigation continues into a boating accident on the Squamish River that left three people dead during heavy rains on Thursday.
 Police respond to a boating accident on the Squamish River on Thursday that left three people dead. (CBC)
 Rainfall warnigns are also in effect for northern, inland and the western Vancouver Island
 Tofino and areas further south could see 120 millimetres of rain, while the area between Zeballos, Gold River and Port Alice could see up to 150 millimetres.
 A number of properties in Zeballos remain under an evacuation order following a landslide triggered amid rainstorms last week .
 Northern, western and central Vancouver Island also remain under high streamflow advisories.
 Coastal flooding advisories are in place for the Metro Vancouver, Greater Victoria, Saanich Inlet and Georgia Strait shorelines through Sunday, with storm surges and strong winds expected to push tides higher than typical levels. 
 Wind warnings are also in effect for most of Vancouver Island, with the exception of the east coast from Nanaimo south to Shawnigan Lake, as well as the Southern Gulf Islands, the Sunshine Coast from Saltery Bay to Powell River, and Haida Gwaii.
 With files from Ivan de Jacquelin
